prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Combine the two independently-successful mechanisms: keep the parent's CTS sink clustering (size=1, diameter=50) and additionally fine-tune it modestly (x2 diameter to 100) so clustered sinks still avoid long clock-detour while reducing buffer/routing pressure — a small coefficient step on the best-known knob rather than a new mechanism.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.057 robust(mean-std)=-0.060 min_case=-0.064 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.029 dWNS=+0.4% dTNS=-4.8% overflow~87
  bp-ng45: score=-0.064 dWNS=-12.9% dTNS=-2.1% overflow~69
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.036 dWNS=-0.8% dTNS=+6.6% overflow~148
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis did not hold: total score is negative (-0.057) and robustly so (mean-std -0.060), with all three cases valid. The modest diameter x2 step hurt bp-ng45 most (dWNS -12.9%), while bp_fe-ng45 improved slightly (+0.036, dTNS +6.6%) and ariane133-ng45 was mildly negative. Plausible mechanism: doubling diameter over-clusters sinks, adding detour/buffer pressure that outweighs routing savings on the sensitive bp case. Next step: sweep diameter between 50 and 100 (e.g., 60/75) per-case rather than a single global x2, and gate the change to cases where overflow is high.
